rationale: The workflow already implements the two most applicable evidence-supported optimizations: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE via the concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true, and P-LIT-GHA-CACHE via existing actions/cache steps for Clang/LLVM, ccache, and apt packages. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated because the build-jank matrix contains independent required build configurations (lint, debug+analysis+coverage, undefined-behavior sanitizer, release on Ubuntu and macOS) where every matrix outcome is needed for full build and test coverage; cancelling remaining cells on failure would hide results and reduce coverage. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks representative successful-duration history to justify new limits, and the long clang build jobs (200-minute timeouts) need their existing headroom. Remaining patterns (Bazel, Python pip, Gradle, environment cache, distributed cache) do not apply to this C++/Clang workflow, and no change would preserve intended coverage while being supported by evidence.
